title: Engram call limits: abort only after 60 s, warn after 10 s (Greg's rule), starting with the acceptance-evaluation submission
outcome: Operation-aborting limits on TermAl's Engram calls follow Greg's rule: abort only after 60 s, and log a warning after 10 s without aborting. The acceptance-evaluation submission is covered first, and the retained evaluations record.
acceptance: The acceptance-evaluation submission into Engram is aborted only after 60 s; a submission still running after 10 s logs a warning naming the operation and the elapsed time without aborting; the attempt key and replay semantics are unchanged, so a resend after an unknown outcome is a replay under the same key.

Every operation-aborting deadline on TermAl's Engram calls (every user of ENGRAM_WORK_BINDING_COMMAND_TIMEOUT, comparable fixed call deadlines, and any outer request or background budget that would abort such a call sooner) is listed on this item with its value and caller; each one shorter than 60 s is raised to at least 60 s with the 10 s warning, longer ones are unchanged, and where the minimum is believed to cause a real problem the evidence is recorded on this item for Greg without introducing an exception. Escalation after an already-issued stop, and retry cadence, are not operation-aborting limits and are out of scope.

Behavioural tests with scaled thresholds and fixture calls, never real 60-second waits, show that a call slower than the warning threshold but faster than the abort threshold succeeds and logs the warning, and that a call past the abort threshold fails with the existing unknown-outcome handling.
After the change is landed and the host restarted, at least one TermAl-project acceptance evaluation submission made on that build is recorded in the tracker.
